This game is a lot of fun, not many players at the moment though.

I have a bit of feedback for the game mechanics.

The AI NPCs never run or powerwalk so it is very obvious when a human player is moving around, I really think they should add some sporadic running/powerwalking with NPCs to help blend in more.

It feels like the guards have 360 degree vision, even when they are far away and not looking they will catch you, it would be nice if they didn't have eyes in the back of their heads.

Perhaps this isn't a problem in other countries, but I couldn't get a single game going with any human players. I'm in Australia, and the server browser only yielded a smattering of 300ms+ ping games. I'm mainly putting the review here because of the complete dearth of players, which is something to keep in mind.

As far as the game goes... sadly, it's a little shallow compared to The Ship. The gameplay more or less consists of focusing on the UI and moving between vignettes, scrapping the more open "last seen" approach in its predecessor. The combat consists of one-hit kills or a thorough scolding, and often the auto-target isn't exactly intuitive. This is paired with the fact that characters don't collide, so you can literally stab somebody through a guard without alerting them. Ranged combat is nonexistent. 

I was going to wait a little longer before refunding, but unfortunately I don't see the main issue (not enough players) resolving itself any time soon. Unfortunate, but still, I would honestly rather play The Ship (not Remasted...)

Despite negative reviews, there really isn't much here to hate. Sure, the game had a bit of a rocky start with bugs and server hosting, but it's grown to be much more than that. It's a great game by design, an action murder mystery arcade game of cat and mouse; only difference is you're not only the cat, but also the mouse.

The only faults with this game can be summarized in three different categories: Minor bugs, population, and neglect. First point is bugs, there aren't very many in 2020 aside from a guard bug that freezes the player when too many actions are preformed. However, this bug isn't very common, out of 120 games, it may only happen 10 times, and only if the players are rowdy enough to cause it to happen. Among bot players, it is far more common, but I don't believe they count towards my point. Another bug would be the visual bug when assassinating someone from a vignette that contains any holdable entity like a pie or a tankard. Once a kill is executed from one of these vignettes, the entity in your hands has a chance to despawn since it is replaced with the murder weapon for a few seconds. Moving an inch will fix this however.

In terms of population, as of today, the player peak was 109 for Murderous Pursuits. Take this as you will, but the game isn't as popular as it once was. The all-time peak for this game was 144,294 back when it first came to be, and I don't believe it will ever rise back to it's formal glory. Despite this however, the game can still be thoroughly enjoyed with friends or with the in-game AI. In terms of AI, MP does an excellent job with their artificial intelligence. The AI acts as real players most of the time, and are very immersive. Sometimes, the AI will feign lag to simulate real people, and it puts a smile on my face. Although the population is low, the AI makes up for this loss, as well as friends to play this game with. The game used to be priced at $20, and is now much more accessible at $10. If you have cash to spare, it's worth the fun.

Now for my final point, neglect. Don't get me wrong, the game is wonderful, but there's a lot of dents that need to be ironed out. The game hasn't been updated in a very long time, and it's fairly evident by the fact that the DLC Mr. X Edition skins have not been added to the newer 8 characters, nor has the 'Mask' victory pose been updated for the 8 new characters. When you purchase the Deluxe Edition, you are only getting skins and poses for half of the characters, whether or not this is worth it is up to the buyer. I would also like to point out that when playing MP, the common player may find the overpoweredness of the Flash and the Counter. These are abilities that I'm sure would be nerfed or reworked if the game had a larger playerbase. A lot of the abilities could use a rework, an example being that Humiliation is less effective than Disguise in the fact that Humiliation gives less points, and is more risky. High risk low reward is not a good incentive to use an ability, especially if it's actually a detriment in most if not all gamemodes thanks to it's exposure destroying capabilities. This is not to say that these overpowered abilities can't be countered, if you're a seasoned player it's easy to spot when these abilities are in use most of the time, and Flash can be sidestepped if you act quick enough. But it's often not quick enough in most situations, depending on how the Flash is used. In theory, it's possible to avoid overpowered abilities, but a gameplay tweak would be much appreciated.

With these points aside, this game is still one of my top favourites in terms of replayability. A lot of people will tell you it's repetitive, but depending on what company you have over, it can be one of the greatest party games out there to enjoy with all of your friends. I give this game a 7/10, it's come a long way from 2018, and it's much better for it. However it is unfortunate to see a game like this go abandoned by it's community, and minorly neglected by it's developers due to this fact. Amazing game, tragic happenstance. 7/10.

Outside of the fact that nobody plays this game (and you thus have to resort to bots), the gameplay changes really don't make for a fun experience. Everything has been streamlined to make the rounds go faster and the gameplay smoother, but in doing this they have removed a lot of what made The Ship special.
Quarries aren't just a once in a round thing, you just get a new one when you die for any reason, so there is very little tension. 
Weapons work on a 1-5 star system instead of a continously increasing money counter, they are also all, in essence, the same weapon. There are no guns, no wallet bombs, no poison. Everything is melee.
Add to this the new special skills weapon, and it just becomes too easy. The only difficulty in the game, strangely, comes from trying to figure out who your quarry even is, because it is intentionally obfuscated.
This was done for the new "blend in" mechanic (lifted straight from Spy Party) which allows you to try and "blend in" with the various NPC's around the ship. 
Problem is, there is very little incentive to do this (you only get a few more points, but this can be avoided with special skills) and it is quite often immediatly obvious who is an NPC and who is not, so it also doesn't work to hide.

The game is not worth 20 bucks, the game isn't even worth 5. I fear at this point the dev's should just stop trying to reboot The Ship. It was a really fun game and I love it dearly, but every attempt Blazing Griffin has made at rebooting the series has failed.

They can become temporarily distracted, during which time hostile actions can take place near the guard.  Where things get silly is that you can be arrested for attempting to stun someone hunting you in front of a guard.  The guard then scribbles in his notebook, which means he is "distracted".  The hunter that the guard prevented you from stunning now kills you literally a foot away from the guard as they continue scribbling.

If you can avoid that bit of silliness, it's definitely worth a few bucks on sale.  Servers are empty, so grab a few friends to play with.  It does have bots if you have no friends, but they don't pose much of a challenge.

As someone who has played many hundreds of hours of the Assassin's Creed multiplayer (which is now, sadly, all but dead), I wasn't going to pass this game by, so here are my first impressions.

- Blazing Griffin obviously did not have the same kind of budget as Ubisoft, so don't expect any flashy animations, but the game looks decent, and the levels are very large and complex. Lots of potential there.

- The soundtrack consists of a single track, and it is some kind of elevator music. Needs to be replaced ASAP.

- My Xbox One controller does not work in the game. Major flaw that needs to be fixed.

- The gameplay mechanics are very similar to Assassin’s Creed, but there are differences:

1) You do not have your target’s picture and have to rely solely on the compass. Given that there are fewer personas and no large crowds like in AC, that is probably a good idea.

2) There are several abilities to choose from, but much fewer than in AC, and there is no clear explanation for how some of them work, you have to figure it out by trial and error. Not good.

3) There is no target lock. Not good AT ALL, it is a must in a game of this type.

4) Unlike in AC, where you are exposed only by performing high-profile actions, in this game, your exposure builds over time, and, unless you enter a blend group, you will be automatically exposed. Not a good decision, in my opinion: the player is basically being punished for doing nothing wrong and forced to constantly stop and wait. 

5) Your score depends (among other things) on the type of weapon you use for the kill. Weapons can be picked up from boxes around the level, and their priority changes as the match goes on. Not sure how to feel about this: on the one hand, it adds another layer to the game, but, on the other hand, it distracts you from the hunt proper.

To summarize: the game has potential and is worth picking up, especially if you were into the AC multiplayer. Whether or not that potential will be realized depends on how well the developers listen and how willing they are to make changes to their work.

Going to make a few comparisons to Assassin's Creed. I didn't like The Ship, but I like this.

* Characters stand out just a bit too well among the NPCs; they don't look the same.
* Locking all the skin tint variations behind how many points you get in games is a bad idea; you need those to vary how you look between rounds.
* The guards suck. Having to stop killing/stunning in areas where you might be "arrested" and then subsequently stunned or killed is a pain. Made trickier because the guards go to sleep and wake up. This all adds nothing and restricts the game's momentum.
* You can pick up weapons to get more points for a kill, but I don't see the point in adding weapons to the game in this way. This is still better than the Ship's awkward implementation.
* You don't earn levels/XP/favour in private games, which is ridiculous (Edit: this has since been fixed). If you're in Australia or another minor region, you're forced to play on high ping servers (about 120-150ms) to get it.  Levels/XP don't seem to do anything, only favour matters for unlocks.
* The devs haven't been responsive on their discord server, even for basic gameplay questions. It's strange, because it's actually a pretty well set up discord server by the look of it.

The devs should look into all of these issues to make a better game.

After coming off of the beta and playing the fully released game I can easily say this game is a worthy follow up to The Ship. I feel Murderous Pursuits really hones the gameplay to a slower more methodical game of cat and mouse. 

After recieving a target you can make sure you are well equipped with the highest scoring weapon and hunt that target down to achieve max points in order to get first in the round. The added feature of using 2 abilities that have cool downs really helps advance the gameplay mechanics into a more thoughtful experience instead of a "shootem up" that The Ship could get into pretty quickly. 

Beware though because not only do you have a target to kill but someone has you as a target as well... So you want to be watchful and try to counter your hunter before they can get the best of you. Sometimes though you will have 2 hunters on your tail. 

The gameplay of Murderous Pursuits also channels parts of the old Assassins Creed multiplayer as well, and that I truly loved playing! Sadly that went away so it is so good to see something like this come about. 

What I would really like to see in this game is something else to do in regards to being forced to do something so you do not get spotted. In this you have a timer that runs out the longer you move in public without blending in, so it adds a point of tension in monitoring what you do at all times. But I would love to see some other elements added in this like in the ship having to watch several meters of varying importance while being on the hunt and being hunted. 

But all in all this game truly is a fun and unique experience! It may be a litle lighter on content but I hope more content will be rolled out over time as more players come into the game. See you at the party ;)

If you're a fan to The Ship, Murderous Pursuits improves on The Ship in several ways. It gets players into the action a lot faster while keeping the key elements of the mystery murder party genere.

The mechanical changes:

- The time investment in the tutorial is far less. You aren't forced to play through a mock level to be guided through all of the mechanisms of the game. I really appriciated this change.

- Removed the "personal needs" mechanism present in The Ship (where you needed to eat, rest, bathe, etc.) to look unsuspicious and instead added the vignettes as a way to do the same. Vigniettes (blending in) also help you improve your score if you manage to track down your quarry, and ignoring them (not blending in) can make you easier to find by those hunting you.

- They removed the prision element while keeping the gards in. When you're caught by guards it exposes you to your hunters as a penalty instead of removing you from the game in a "time out". 

- Weapons are simplified. Instead of having to look through a long list and figure out which weapon is most valuable, the game removes the list shrinks the number of options (not a bad thing in this case) and displays the value of the weapons over them when you are playing. This helps you keep your attention in the game and on your surroundings. Weapon location is also reliable so you don't have to rely on luck as much if you can learn where the weapons are.

- Level designs appear to be limited to two levels of elevation

- Character population in the levels is much higher.

I think that this iteration of the mystery murder party is far more streamlined than The Ship (which I enjoyed). I enjoyed getting into the game quickly, the controls were easy to pick up, and the interface is pretty clean. It is not as heavy, mechanically as The Ship which may turn you away if you liked the big levels and the larger weapon options. However I would argue that simplifying the formula removes a barrier to entry. I did not think The Ship could be jumped into with cold feet, whereas this title could be with less growing pains.

And I think that this is important because the title seems to be suffering from the low population that The Ship did. I would reccomend not letting that stop you. Instead, find some friends who are interested, and give this one a try. 

I don't think Murderous Pursuits deserves a thumbs down just because server population is suffering. There are a lot of positive changes to the formula worth checking out.

Overall, if you're into multiplayer games that basis is investigative/stealthy in nature, I would give this a try. 

However, I do categorize this as a definite rage-inducer. I can't critique the abilities that exist for exisiting, because they are neccessary, but they are essentially broken due to the fact that you can activate an ability first, but the other person's ability will be inacted instead due to lag or ping differences. This is cause for confusion and anger due to fact winning a duel seems like luck of the draw. 

But more than that, my biggest critique and probably what may disuade most people from buying this game is that there is no functional party system. The only way to garuntee you play with a friend is to join a game (which has a very short timer) and quickly invite your friend before it runs out. I've been playing The Ship games since it was a mod for Half Life. I'm enjoying this version as it gets rid of the, by today's standards, poorly designed needs. Needs were implemented in the mod, continuing to later the source and remaster editions, as a way of forcing players to move around the map to open them up for attack. However, because of the arbitrary nature of the needs, you would often find yourself having to go into the opposite direction of your own quarry which was often very frustrating.

In Murderous Pursuits they narrowed and polished the scope of needs to be more player controlled and of use to avoid both the scanning eyes of quarry and hunter. Now you blend in areas they in the past would be designated as food or entertainment while still having a penalty for not using them; move around too long or too fast without stopping to blend in and you’ll be exposed to all players on the map with an icon denoting you for both your quarry and hunter to see even through walls. People should not get hung up on the removal of needs as, at best, they were a façade of depth; arbitrary mechanics that added nothing to the game while making it more difficult and obtuse for newer players to join.

Gone are the previous versions many, and often unneeded, variety of weapons as well. For those who remember The Ship: Source and players over reliance on the axe or other high damage weapon for self-defense there is no longer anything similar in Murderous Pursuits. No more searching containers and finding five blunt weapons all with the same damage but none being the current that Mr. X wants you to use for a high payout. No longer are ranged weapons vastly superior to all melee weapons due to the ability to shoot into safely patrolled or camera covered areas. The weapons all behave the same and the only difference is how Mr. X will award you for using them. You must be close and personal to your target, waiting for them to pass by a vantage point you’ve blended into for the perfect moment or waiting for that critical moment to rush into a room and drive a knife into their neck. Relying on RNG to get an advantageous weapon is gone; the only difference between player’s is their skill at being stealthy and blending in. There is no longer a crutch of an axe or blunderbuss to ruin a better player’s well laid trapped simply because you hit the RNG lotto on a certain cabinet.

In the end Murderous Pursuits trims off a long lot of the rough and superficial appearance of depth to allow the true depth, the one that all the versions of The Ship and Bloody Good time, that drew their cult followings. By removing the chaff and poorly implemented design choices the more refined Murderous Pursuits still has the game play loop that attracted previous fan bases and offers a softer curve thanks to the design team learning from previous games that allows new players to this type of gameplay to be able to engage with more seasoned hunters instead of bouncing off a sheer wall. All in all, as someone who’s been with The Ship and its variants since their inception, this is a very worthy successor to them.

This game does a few things right, and a few things just drastically wrong. 

If you want the feeling of paranoid cat/mouse gameplay, you won't find it here. They tell you when you have line of sight of your pursuers, which means with some basic observational skills it's child's play to determine who is hunting you. With the defensive abilities you can use it often becomes more effective to farm stuns off your pursuer than to go hunt your target.

If you want the feeling of stalking your target, you might find it but it won't be fulfilling. Unlike Assassin's Creed, this game does *not* tell you what your target looks like. This would be an interesting decision if it weren't for the aforementioned ability to tell who your pursuer is easily. Once you know who you're hunting, they almost certainly know who you are, leading to a Mexican stand off where you both try to bait each other into traps until someone slips and dies.

The map design itself isn't bad, but there's a consistent mechanic that seems out of place: The guard.

If a guard is watching and you draw your weapon (Even to stun your pursuer) the guard will arrest you, broadcasting your location to your hunters and target. The guard will then stop watching for a bit. This serves no purpose other than to slow the game down.

One ability, pie bomb, fundamentally breaks the cat/mouse gameplay. Pie bombs are land mines that exist for 45 seconds (with 1  minute cooldown starting when you place it down) and explode if your target or hunters walk near them. If your hunters walk near them, it's an automatic stun, netting you 3 easy points. If your target walks into it, it kills them for about 10 points.  It's frankly just ridiculous, and the counterplay is very limited.

This game is the best game available for what it is, but it falls short of what it needs to be. Because of that, I cannot recommend this game.

This is a game of kill or be killed. To win, you'll have to outplay your rivals, use tactics of your own, blend in with the crowd. Set on board a Victorian-era ship, you get to play in one of several ship-board locations and must identify and kill another player among the passengers, without drawing too much attention to yourself or having the guards witnessing the act.

It's a rather watered down version of AC:Brotherhood's multiplayer experience. The levels often feature two stories, but are essentially flat, as there aren't any acrobatics or jumping in the game. The levels are also quite small, but since there aren't any advanced movement mechanics in the game, larger levels would be too unwieldy. Even in spite of the levels' small size, they are not very populated. Most of the NPCs congregate in the rooms leaving the walking paths / cooridors very empty, making it very easy to be discovered while moving from place to place. The abilities are also not very polished. Smoke bomb is pretty much useless, since it's hard to find another NPC that looks exactly like your character... Also experienced hitches/latency issues during gameplay, which wasn't very enjoyable, and there aren't enough people playing to find a server with a better connection. All abillities are unlocked from the get-go so there's zero progression loop in the game, so there's nothing to keep me coming back for more. Pretty shallow experience overall :-(
